```{python}
# Shared body of the country pages: the including page sets COUNTRY first.
from IPython.display import HTML
import charts
import pagedata

page = pagedata.Page(COUNTRY)
df, sig, res = page.facts, page.sig, page.reserved
top = charts.top_block_sector(df)
top_label = charts.SECTOR_LABELS.get(top["sector"], top["sector"])
all_block = charts._block_agg(df, "GPTBot")
all_block_pct = f"{100 * all_block['blk'].sum() / all_block['tot'].sum():.1f}%"

offer = sig.assign(n=sig["observable_llms_hand"] + sig["observable_llms_generated"])
offer = offer.assign(share=offer["n"] / offer["observable"]).sort_values(
    ["share", "n"], ascending=False).iloc[0]
offer_label = charts.SECTOR_LABELS.get(offer["sector"], offer["sector"])
offer_plain = int(offer["observable_llms_hand"])

reserve_sectors = charts.reserve_by_sector(res)
trend = pagedata.trend(page.panel, COUNTRY)


def as_table(t, filename):
    """Table view of a chart's data — same numbers, no hover needed, and
    downloadable as CSV."""
    return HTML(charts.table_html(t, filename))
```

## Block {#block}

Sites keep AI crawlers out through **robots.txt** — a plain-text file that can
name a crawler and disallow paths. The chart above counts only the rules that
name GPTBot.

Crawler by crawler: each bar is one crawler and splits into how the
`{python} page.n_observed` sites we could read treat it: **blocked** at the
root, **partial** (some paths off limits), or **allowed**.
`{python} page.n_unobserved` sites blocked our crawler, failed with a server
error or answered from another site; they have no verdict and are left out of
every share on this page. Every bar is a whole, so the figures inside it are
shares of sites, not counts — the counts are in the tooltip and the table. Use
the menus to slice by sector, or by whether a rule *names the crawler* or comes
from a catch-all `*`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Offer {#offer}

The opposite move. **llms.txt** (a 2024 convention) is a Markdown file that
*offers* a curated view of a site to language models — "here is what to read
about us." **`{python} page.n_llms` of `{python} page.n_observed` sites,
`{python} page.pct(page.n_llms)`**, publish one. The highest share is in
**`{python} offer_label`**: `{python} int(offer["n"])` of
`{python} int(offer["observable"])` sites, `{python} offer_plain` of them with
no plugin signature.

The chart counts only those `{python} page.n_llms` publishers and splits each
sector by where the file seems to come from: ink for a file with no plugin
signature, gray for a plugin default. A missing signature suggests a decision
rather than a side effect; it does not prove one. Sector sizes are in the table.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Reserve {#reserve}

The legal one. Under EU copyright law (Directive 2019/790, Article 4), AI
companies may text-and-data-mine public content for training **unless the owner
reserves the right in a machine-readable form**. **TDMRep** is that reservation —
the only one of the three signals with legal weight in the EU. A site counts
when it states `tdm-reservation: 1` in any of the protocol's three channels.

```{python}
HTML(charts.reserve_stat(page))
```

Every site that reserves, and the channel it signals through:

```{python}

```

## Method {#method}

**The sample.** `{python} page.n_domains` `{python} page.names["adj"]` websites
across `{python} page.n_sectors` sectors (sample version
`{python} page.sample`). A site belongs to a country when it is aimed mainly at
that country's audience, whatever its domain: national sites on `.com` count.
Each host is counted in one place only; hosts that serve several countries on a
par sit in a separate international list. Sector sizes follow Italy's
proportions in every country; sample sizes follow each country's count in the
Tranco top-1M list, dampened so the largest countries do not dominate. The rules and every borderline call are in
[sample/METHOD.md](https://github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census/blob/main/sample/METHOD.md).

**The three signals.** For every site we fetch and *validate* three files:

- **robots.txt**, parsed under RFC 9309 (longest-match, `Allow` wins ties). A
  crawler's verdict is **blocked** when the root path is denied, **partial**
  when only some paths are, **allowed** otherwise. A rule is *specific* when the
  site names the crawler's exact token, *wildcard* when it comes from a
  catch-all `User-agent: *`.
- **llms.txt**, a Markdown file offering content to models. A *plugin default*
  carries a generator's signature or copies the site's llms-full.txt.
- **TDMRep**, the EU legal reservation, read through all three channels of the
  protocol (a well-known file, HTTP headers, and HTML meta tags).

**Presence is validated, never assumed.** A `200 OK` proves nothing — many
servers answer 200 with an HTML page on any path. A file counts only if it is
structurally valid; soft-404s are excluded, and a bot-protection page served in
place of robots.txt makes the site unobservable.

**Observability.** All fetches run from one address in Italy. Sites that block
non-browser clients, refuse foreign visitors (several betting sites), fail with
a server error or redirect to another site have no verdict and are left out of
every share: counting them as allowing crawlers would invent a policy.

**Limits.** robots.txt measures *declared intent*, not crawler behaviour. The
CMS/plugin fingerprint is heuristic. "Not mentioned" is a default, not a
decision, and is kept separate from explicit permission throughout.

**Data & code.** `{python} page.n_crawlers` AI crawlers are tracked. The full
pipeline and the snapshot data, aggregated and per domain, are open:
[github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census](https://github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census).
